introduction_markdown:
Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board, General Certificate of Education Examination, ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2019. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2, subject code 0575. Time allowed: two and a half hours.

Answer ALL QUESTIONS IN SECTION A and ANY TWO QUESTIONS FROM EITHER SECTION B or SECTION C. In Sections B and C, ALL QUESTIONS CARRY EQUAL MARKS. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three.

Section A: Pure Mathematics (compulsory to all candidates, answer all questions). Section B: Mechanics (answer any two questions; if this section is chosen, then Section C may not be chosen). Section C: Statistics and Probability (if this section is chosen, then Section B may not be chosen; answer any two questions).

All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators may be used. Where necessary take $g$ as $10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.
incertitudes: Section B/C : la consigne imprimee (reponse a deux questions de la Section B OU de la Section C, jamais un melange des trois) n'est pas exprimable par les regles de choix (« parmi 2 sur 3 » par section) ; elle est recopiee en entier dans l'introduction. Chaque question de B et C vaut 17 points imprimes (egalite annoncee par le sujet).
Q9 : le sujet imprime « (i), (iii), (iii) » ; la deuxieme partie est renumerotee (ii) (faute de numerotation). Points imprimes 3 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 1 + 3 + 2 = 17, conformes.

Q9(i) : « moves from a fixed point O with velocity 12 m/s » interprete comme vitesse initiale 12 m/s a t = 0 (la vitesse ne s'annule qu'a t = 2 puis t = 6, donc pas de retour avant t = 2 : distance = deplacement).

Q9(iii) : DONNEES INCOHERENTES. Avec S (3 kg, 2 m/s) et T (2 kg, 5 m/s) en sens contraires, la quantite de mouvement de T (10) depasse celle de S (6) : la vitesse commune est 0,8 m/s dans le sens de T, et non « dans le sens de S » comme l'annonce le sujet. Corrige donne pour les donnees imprimees (0,8 m/s dans le sens de T) avec la remarque ; si les vitesses etaient permutees (S 5 m/s, T 2 m/s), on obtiendrait 2,2 m/s dans le sens de S. La perte d'energie cinetique (29,4 J) est la meme dans les deux lectures. Aucune lecture n'est choisie arbitrairement.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) A particle moves in a straight line from a fixed point, $O$ with velocity $12\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and after $t$ seconds of motion, the acceleration, $a=(2t-8)\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.

Find:

(a) the velocity of the particle when $t=2$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Velocity is the integral of acceleration:

$$
v=\int(2t-8)\,dt=t^2-8t+c
$$

At $t=0$, $v=12$, so $c=12$ and $v=t^2-8t+12$.

At $t=2$: $v=4-16+12=0$.

**The velocity at $t=2$ is $0\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$** (the particle is instantaneously at rest).

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) the distance of the particle from $O$ when $t=2$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Distance is the integral of velocity, with $s=0$ at $t=0$ (the particle starts at $O$):

$$
s=\int(t^2-8t+12)\,dt=\frac{t^3}{3}-4t^2+12t
$$

At $t=2$:

$$
s=\frac{8}{3}-16+24=\frac{8}{3}+8=\frac{32}{3}
$$

Since $v=(t-2)(t-6)>0$ for $0<t<2$, the particle does not turn back before $t=2$, so the distance equals the displacement.

**The particle is $\dfrac{32}{3}\ \mathrm{m}\approx10.7\ \mathrm{m}$ from $O$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) A particle $P$, of mass $4\ \mathrm{kg}$, is connected by a light inelastic string, which passes over a fixed light smooth pulley to a particle of mass $m\ \mathrm{kg}$ where $m>4$. The string is taut and the particles are released from rest. Given that the acceleration of each particle is $2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$,

Find:

(a) the tension in the string, *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Take $g=10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. Since $m>4$, the particle $P$ ($4$ kg) moves **up** with acceleration $2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ and the particle $m$ moves **down** with the same acceleration (inelastic string, same tension $T$ throughout over a smooth pulley).

Newton's second law for $P$ (upward positive):

$$
T-4g=4\times2\ \Rightarrow\ T=40+8=48
$$

**The tension in the string is $48\ \mathrm{N}$.**

Newton's second law for the particle of mass $m$ (downward positive):

$$
mg-T=m\times2\ \Rightarrow\ 10m-48=2m\ \Rightarrow\ 8m=48\ \Rightarrow\ m=6
$$

This satisfies $m>4$.

**$m=6$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) the force exerted on the pulley. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The string pulls the pulley downward with tension $T$ on each side, so the resultant force on the (light, smooth) pulley is

$$
2T=2\times48=96\ \mathrm{N}
$$

**The force exerted on the pulley is $96\ \mathrm{N}$, acting vertically downwards.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(iii) Two particles $S$ and $T$, of masses $3\ \mathrm{kg}$ and $2\ \mathrm{kg}$ respectively, are moving towards each other in a straight line with velocities $2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and $5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ respectively. The particles collide, coalesce and move in the direction of $S$. Calculate:

(a) their common velocity after collision, *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Conservation of momentum, taking the direction of $S$ as positive (so $T$ has velocity $-5$):

$$
3(2)+2(-5)=(3+2)v\ \Rightarrow\ 6-10=5v\ \Rightarrow\ v=-\frac45=-0.8
$$

The common velocity is $-0.8\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$: its size is $0.8\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and it is directed **opposite to the direction of $S$**, that is in the direction of $T$ (the momentum of $T$, $10$, is larger than that of $S$, $6$).

**Common velocity: $0.8\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ in the direction of $T$.**

*Remark:* the printed statement says that the particles move in the direction of $S$, which does not agree with these data. If the velocities were the other way round ($S$ at $5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $T$ at $2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$), the same method gives $\dfrac{15-4}{5}=2.2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ in the direction of $S$.

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) the loss in kinetic energy after collision. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Kinetic energy before: $\dfrac12(3)(2)^2+\dfrac12(2)(5)^2=6+25=31\ \mathrm{J}$.

Kinetic energy after (mass $5$ kg, speed $0.8\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$): $\dfrac12(5)(0.8)^2=1.6\ \mathrm{J}$.

$$
\text{Loss}=31-1.6=29.4\ \mathrm{J}
$$

(The loss is also $29.4\ \mathrm{J}$ if the velocities are swapped as in the remark above: $41.5-12.1=29.4$.)

**The loss in kinetic energy is $29.4\ \mathrm{J}$.**
